- [ASSISTANT_SAID] 3. Popularity does not necessarily translate to votes; a candidate may be well-liked but lack the resources to effectively run a campaign.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] 4. Research has shown that the candidate with more money often wins the election.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] 5. Money allows candidates to reach a wider audience and persuade voters through targeted advertising and messaging.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] 6. Money can be used to fund negative campaigning against opponents, damaging their reputation and swaying voters.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] 7. While popularity may help a candidate, it is ultimately the financial resources that can make or break a campaign.
